failing_checks.title: Per-action amount bound
failing_checks.reason: The client signs whatever amount the challenge states, with no maximum. The server fee bump is also uncapped (fee*10 from the client-supplied inner fee).

failing_checks.title: Cumulative budget
failing_checks.reason: The client has no cumulative or daily budget. Many small challenges are each paid.

failing_checks.title: Atomic budget accounting
failing_checks.reason: The cumulative amount is read at line 195 and written at line 287 with an await between them, with no lock. Concurrent verifies both pass. The replay get/put is also non-atomic.

failing_checks.title: Recipient binding
failing_checks.reason: The client pays the recipient named in the challenge, with no allowlist.

failing_checks.title: Replay and double payment
failing_checks.reason: Replay protection is keyed only on the challenge id, and only if a store is configured. The tx hash is never recorded as used.

failing_checks.title: Incoming payment verification
failing_checks.reason: Destination, asset and amount are checked, but the proof is not bound to the challenge or payer, and a hash can be reused.

failing_checks.title: Externally supplied transactions
failing_checks.reason: The client signs a transfer built from the challenge's amount, currency and recipient. It applies no cap or allowlist. prepareTransaction output from the RPC is signed without inspection.

failing_checks.title: Raw byte signing
failing_checks.reason: The signed bytes come from a contract and RPC the challenge selects, and are signed raw.

failing_checks.title: Network and endpoint pinning
failing_checks.reason: The challenge picks the network, which sets the passphrase and the RPC URL, on both client signing paths.

failing_checks.title: Expiry and fees
failing_checks.reason: The fee-bump fee is 10 times the client-supplied inner fee, with no cap. Transactions do carry timeouts.

failing_checks.title: Submission outcome
failing_checks.reason: The `sendResult.status` field (ERROR, TRY_AGAIN_LATER, DUPLICATE) is never checked, in server Charge, channel close, close() or client push. The code goes straight to polling by hash. A rejected send is polled for 60s before an unhelpful error. If the transaction lands after the 60 polls, the thrown

failing_checks.title: Failure and rollback paths
failing_checks.reason: The challenge replay marker is written before verification, so any failure burns the challenge. The cumulative amount is stored before the close transaction is submitted. If close fails, the store is left inconsistent with the chain. The read-then-write is non-atomic.

failing_checks.title: Verification of incoming authentication
failing_checks.reason: The signature is checked correctly against the single commitment key. However, the cumulative read, verify and write sequence is not atomic. Concurrent credentials can both pass against the same previous cumulative, and a `close` can replay. The earlier finding covers this.

failing_checks.title: Controls outside the prompt
failing_checks.reason: The client signs whatever amount, currency, recipient and network the challenge names. No code-enforced cap or allowlist exists. The channel server also continues when the on-chain closed check fails.
